The Lost World of the Indus Valley

How did the Indus people live, and why did their great cities disappear? Follow the trail after finding the archaeologist's satchel.

The story so far

The Lost Archaeologist

Many years ago, an archaeologist set out to solve one of history's biggest mysteries: why did the great cities of the Indus Valley disappear?

For years she dug at ancient sites along the Indus River. She studied their culture: what the people ate, how they built their cities, what they made with their hands and how they traded.

Then one night, she vanished. All she left behind was her leather satchel, an old map and a journal with six sites circled in red.

Now you have found the satchel. Follow her trail to all six sites. At each site, use the sources in the satchel to prove that her notes are right.

But be careful. A rival treasure hunter wants the satchel too. He will try to trick you at every step.

The archaeologist left a claim on the map. Your job is to find the evidence that backs it up.

THE CLAIM
  1. Read the claim. A claim is something a person says is true. You need proof.
  2. Open the satchel on the left. Each card is a source, a clue from the past. Tap a card to pin it to the map.
  3. Pin 3 sources that support the claim. A red string connects each one to the claim. A solid string means it fits. A dashed string means there is a problem.
  4. Answer the rival. He will question your sources. If a source does not support the claim, cut the string. If he is wrong, prove it with your lantern.
  5. Write the conclusion in the journal. Choose the sentence the evidence supports best.
Use your worksheet. Fill in each part of your worksheet as you finish it. Watch your torch. Every wrong move puts out one flame. Read each card carefully before you pin it.  Stuck? Tap 🔊 Read to me, or tap ? How to play.
